title: Six Metrics To Track For Car Wash Marketing - SLAM Car Wash Marketing

facts.fact: The SLAM Car Wash Marketing article states that a CPM below $5 is a win for brand awareness campaigns.
facts.quote: Generally speaking, anything less than $5 CPM is a win.

facts.fact: The article defines CPM as cost per thousand impressions.
facts.quote: CPM (Cost Per Millie, or Cost Per Thousand Impressions)

facts.fact: In its ROAS example, SLAM uses an illustrative average car wash ticket price of $14.
facts.quote: let's say our average ticket price at a car wash is $14.

facts.fact: In its ROAS example, SLAM uses an Unlimited Plan price of $30 per month.
facts.quote: converted 10% of that traffic into the Unlimited Plan at $30 a month, with a 10 month average member cycle

facts.fact: In its ROAS example, SLAM assumes a 10-month average member cycle.
facts.quote: with a 10 month average member cycle

facts.fact: In its ROAS example, SLAM assumes 300 people were driven to the wash in one month by Google and Waze ads.
facts.quote: If Google and Waze ads drove 300 people to the wash this month

facts.fact: In its ROAS example, SLAM assumes a 10% conversion of that traffic into the Unlimited Plan.
facts.quote: your sales team converted 10% of that traffic into the Unlimited Plan

facts.fact: In its ROAS example, SLAM calculates the campaign generated $1,780 of business.
facts.quote: that total is $1,780 worth of business that came from this month's ad campaign

facts.fact: In its ROAS example, SLAM states a $11,000 monthly digital ad spend and reports this equals about a 1200% return on ad spend.
facts.quote: if we spent $11,000 this month on that digital ad campaign, then that's about a 1200% return on ad spend

facts.fact: SLAM advises against geo-targeting digital ads with a flat 5-mile radius.
facts.quote: don't just geo-target your ads with a flat 5-mile radius.
